newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rebound on month-end bargain hunters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rebound on month-end bargain hunters.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose Thursday for the first time in five sessions.
The IPC index added 29.86 points, or 0.76 percent, to 3,936.11. Trading volume was meagre at just 47.4 million shares.
"Volume was razor thin, nothing really interesting happened today," one trader said.
Financial firm Bancomer weighed most on the upside and recouped 10 centavos (1 cent) to close at 2.97 pesos (38 cents). The stock accounted for 10 percent of all shares traded during the session.
Retail firm Cifra shares were the most heavily traded, after Bancomer.
Cifra B gained 26 centavos (3 cents) to 13.40 pesos ($1.70), while the C series ended up 22 centavos (3 cents) to 12.42 pesos ($1.57). Technical analysts said the bourse
rebounded above a pyschological barrier at 3,900 points.
A total of 109 stocks traded, with gainers outpacing decliners by 50 to 31.
Situr, tourist arm of the debt-stricken Sidek group, was a prominent gainer and ended up three centavos at 43 centavos.
Dealers said the share rose on speculation a debt restructuring would be announced at a shareholders' meeting on Friday. Sidek shares meanwhile closed unchnaged at 66 centavos (8 cents).
